name: Solifenacin pivotal trial (Cardozo 2004)
question: Does once-daily solifenacin 5 mg or 10 mg reduce micturitions in patients with overactive bladder compared with placebo?

design.population: Adults with overactive bladder symptoms for at least 3 months, at least 8 micturitions per 24 hours, and at least 3 urgency and/or incontinence episodes in a 3-day diary after a 2-week placebo run-in.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 randomized trial
design.locator: Full text, Patients and Methods, p 1920; Results, p 1920

verdictNote: Both doses met the primary micturition endpoint; dry mouth increased with dose.
takeaway: In a 12-week placebo-controlled trial, solifenacin 5 mg and 10 mg once daily reduced mean micturitions per 24 hours more than placebo in patients with overactive bladder; dry mouth was more frequent with solifenacin, especially 10 mg.

reports.label: Primary report
reports.dateLocator: Crossref published-print: November 2004 (day not supplied); PubMed citation: November 2004
reports.citation: Cardozo L, Lisec M, Millard R, et al. "Randomized, double-blind placebo controlled trial of the once daily antimuscarinic agent solifenacin succinate in patients with overactive bladder." *J Urol.* 2004;172(5 Pt 1):1919-1924. doi:10.1097/01.ju.0000140729.07840.16

results.measure: Mean change in micturitions per 24 hours from baseline to 12-week endpoint; efficacy set (286 on 5 mg, 281 on placebo), last observation carried forward; prespecified ANOVA
results.note: The confidence interval is for the between-arm difference, not the within-arm change. Prespecified two-sided alpha was 0.05.
results.locator: Full text, Statistical analysis, p 1920; Results, pp 1920-1921; Table 1, p 1921

results.measure: Mean change in micturitions per 24 hours from baseline to 12-week endpoint; efficacy set (290 on 10 mg, 281 on placebo), last observation carried forward; prespecified ANOVA
results.note: The confidence interval is for the between-arm difference, not the within-arm change. Prespecified two-sided alpha was 0.05.
results.locator: Full text, Statistical analysis, p 1920; Results, pp 1920-1921; Table 1, p 1921

results.measure: Mean change in urgency episodes per 24 hours from baseline to 12 weeks

effect.p: 5 mg versus placebo: 0.003; 10 mg versus placebo: 0.002

results.note: Unadjusted ANOVA comparison; efficacy set (286, 290, and 281 for 5 mg, 10 mg, and placebo). Between-arm 95% CIs: −1.44 to −0.28 (5 mg) and −1.49 to −0.35 (10 mg).
results.locator: Full text, Results, pp 1920-1921; Table 1, p 1921

results.measure: Mean change in nocturia episodes per 24 hours from baseline to 12 weeks

effect.p: 5 mg versus placebo: not significant; 10 mg versus placebo: 0.036

results.note: Unadjusted ANOVA; 10 mg versus placebo difference approximately −0.19 episodes (95% CI −0.38 to −0.01). The 5 mg comparison was not significant.
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 1921; Figure 2, p 1921

results.measure: Mean change in all incontinence episodes per 24 hours at 12-week endpoint; adjusted ANCOVA

effect.p: 5 mg versus placebo: 0.002; 10 mg versus placebo: 0.016

results.note: 491/857 efficacy-set participants (57%) reported incontinence at baseline; P values are from ANCOVA adjusted for baseline. Adjusted placebo change was not reported.
results.locator: Full text, Results, pp 1921-1922; Figure 4, p 1922

results.measure: Mean change in urge-incontinence episodes per 24 hours at 12-week endpoint; adjusted ANCOVA

effect.p: 5 mg versus placebo: 0.014; 10 mg versus placebo: 0.042

results.note: 405/857 efficacy-set participants (47%) reported urge incontinence at baseline; P values are from ANCOVA adjusted for baseline. Adjusted placebo change was not reported.
results.locator: Full text, Results, pp 1921-1922; Figure 4, p 1922

results.measure: Mean change from baseline to 12-week endpoint, mL

effect.p: 5 mg versus placebo: 0.0001; 10 mg versus placebo: 0.0001

results.note: Between-arm differences from rounded changes are approximately +20.1 mL (95% CI 12.4 to 27.7) and +25.3 mL (95% CI 17.7 to 33.0), respectively.
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 1922; Figure 2, p 1921

results.endpoint: Continence among participants incontinent at baseline
results.measure: No incontinence at 12-week endpoint among participants with at least one baseline incontinence episode
results.note: 491/857 efficacy-set participants had incontinence at baseline; arm-specific counts and placebo continence rate were not reported.

delivery.label: Treatment schedule
delivery.value: After a 2-week placebo run-in, oral solifenacin 5 mg or 10 mg, or placebo, was taken once daily for 12 weeks. Of 911 randomized, 907 were treated, 857 entered the efficacy analysis, and 830/907 (91.5%) completed treatment; 3-day micturition diaries preceded visits every 4 weeks.
delivery.locator: Full text, Study design and Results, p 1920; Table 2, p 1921
